A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the entangled value of a game is a robust measure for the value of the game.
we prove a parallel repetition theorem in the quantum setting for a large class of games, which includes the class of XOR games.
the entangled value of any two player one round game G, when the questions (x,y) ∈ X ×Y are drawn from a uniform distribution on X ×Y, is exponentially close to the classical value.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parallel repetition of entangled games can be analyzed in a similar way as that of classical games, without using the techniques of the quantum de Finetti theorem or quantum information measures.
entanglement does not increase the power of the players beyond the parallel repetition theorem for classical games.
the parallel repetition theorem holds even for quantum entangled games, provided the questions to Alice and Bob in the game are drawn from a classical product distribution.
